dedupe_keys.name: gb road traffic counts and annual average daily flows department for transport

description: The Department for Transport collects traffic counts to produce statistics on the level of traffic on roads in Great Britain. Data are published every year for each junction-to-junction link on the major road network (motorways and A roads) and for the sample of count points on the minor road network (B, C and unclassified roads) that are counted each year, in three forms: the raw manual counts made by trained enumerators, annual average daily flows (AADF) for count points on major and minor roads, and traffic figures for local authorities and regions. Coverage is national for Great Britain. The data are free under the Open Government Licence and available to download in bulk as zipped CSV files, together with the major road link network and a metadata note, and to browse street by street on the interactive road traffic statistics site; summary statistics appear annually and quarterly. Caveats: minor roads are covered only by a sample of count points, and methods are described in the road traffic statistics guidance. The link flows support network flow and capacity studies, exposure weighting of road links for hazard and closure analysis, and calibration of transport models. They complement the Bus Open Data Service and the Network Rail open data feeds.
